Lzahlia's "Atlas of Anthropos" is a work-in-process Framework for mapping [[]] and understanding [[163]] and Unifying [[]] isolated Domains of Human inquiry. These include the major-most spheres, Psychology[[]], Phenomenology [[173]]

The story began with a simple question: Has a "Cartography of Human Phenomenology" ever been attempted? Even before the idea was formed; I often ponder about the true nature of the Human Experience; from the Phenomenological lens.

However, Phenomenology has often been treated as a mere branch of "Philosophy of Mind" [[159]]; rendering it's real-world use-cases to the [[59]] Subjective.

Something like an "Atlas of the Anthropos."

I am envisioning an Atlas wherein, rather than "mapping the Human condition" we strategically play towards our Epistemological "Lack of total understanding." A map is a fascinating application for this strategy; as a map is essentially 

I propose at the bedrock, or "beginning" of the map would be the same thing as the "end" of the map; a Telos or "A means towards which all direction is orientated towards." This is somewhat of a fundamental axiomatic assumption that the map should serve some kind of ultimate purpose; not merely studying the Anthropo-centric for means of knowledge, but with the same purpose as a sailor would map uncharted seas; for navigation of the unknown, for in the unknown, is perhaps... That, unintentionally, reads an awful lot like a Mythos or an Archetypal story. I believe the story is the central architecture of the Human experience. The story is not the map; but the paths through which the map is drawn upon. In some sense; a decision is akin to taking one path of a terrain over another. The decision-making process, rationale, or "reason" for taking one path over any number of possible paths, is what we may define as perhaps the most important Human element; Reason or Ethos.

We already see a structure converging here; There is a beginning and an end of the Atlas of the Anthropos.

This atlas also unifies one of the most isolated faculties; the intellect. The Human quest for knowledge, study and understanding. It has largely occupied most of Human history and recent development. Even Christ said "My people perish for lack of knowledge." So knowledge is one core aspect of Human life. However; the atlas itself is not simply a stamp collection of Phenomenology; the purpose of an Atlas is synonymous with Linguistics itself. When we give a name to an emotion, a place, or even a person, we essentially abstract the complex content into a representative form; the abstraction. This is even more significant for Phenomenological aspects; mapping and naming are synonymous. When we name something, it essentially marks the land; "Someone was here before you, this area has already been discovered. Perhaps the terrain still holds more to be discovered, but this specific layer, has been excavated."

The atlas itself encodes the Epistemological problem of "detached Human intellect" at the level of the medium itself; a map is fundamentally representative of a larger complex terrain. It is a cross section of a manifold space, with bias of capture, i.e., level-of-detail, legend, labelling, landmarks, and so forth. Those can be abstracted as "general detail." Most of Human intellect is tunneling deep into the reservoirs of knowledge, study and information, to extract deeper levels of fundamental understanding; we essentially increase the level of resolution at which we are studying life, while descending further into veins of isolated inquiry. That's synonymous with a path;

This is where the Atlas loops back to the begininng, or the Telos; "What is the sytsem of values which drives the Human being to navigate this complex space we call life?"

I envision the Atlas being a conceptual schematic, as much as visualizable. Regardless of format or intepretation, the source is describing a Unification between isolated or hidden parts of the Human experience. To make the invisible, visible... so that it may be studied, understood, mapped and navigated. Where emotion and physiology are interlinked in coherent threads, and where...
